ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, shareholders, authorised signatories, and beneficial owners of the Hong Kong intermediate holding company and the China WFOE must be screened against the OFAC Specialty Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN), the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (where relevant), the PRC Ministry of Public Security domestic wanted and terrorist designations, and the Hong Kong AMLO/UN Sanctions (Hong Kong) lists. The screening must cover PEP status, adverse media, negative regulatory actions, money laundering predicates, and politically exposed persons connected with mainland China, Hong Kong and all other relevant jurisdictions. Screening frequency must be continuous, with re-screening every 30 days and on event-driven triggers. All hits must be escalated to the AML compliance officer for risk acceptance or rejection.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform and the provincial Market Regulation Administration's Name Self-Service Reservation Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every China WFOE must have a legal name in simplified Chinese characters using the statutory four-tier structure: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or operational characteristic + limited liability company legal form suffix (e.g., Limited Liability Company or Co., Ltd.). The name must be approved through SAMR's autonomous name-selection system. A Pinyin or other Romanised transliteration may be used as an additional registered English version for foreign trade and banking convenience, but the simplified Chinese name is the controlling legal name. The transliteration must be phonetically accurate, avoid negative foreign-language connotations, and must not be a mere translation of an existing famous mark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by SAMR's name review system, the applicant must first review the electronic rejection reason in the registration portal. If the applicant believes the rejection is erroneous, it must file a written administrative reconsideration application with the online dispute resolution channel of the same SAMR bureau within 15 days, attaching the preliminary name-clearing search screenshot, the proposed name structure explanation, the business scope, and the constitutionally valid UBO information. The bureau must issue a written reconsideration decision within 7 working days. If still rejected, the applicant may escalate to the next-level SAMR administrative appeal body or, after exhausting administrative remedies, institute an administrative lawsuit at the competent people's court within the statutory limitation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a PRC mainland WFOE engaged in ISIC 4791 direct online retail of portable battery generators and solar panels, a virtual office or commercial mailbox-only registered address is impermissible and will be rejected by the State Taxation Administration (SAT) for VAT and corporate income tax registration, by the People's Bank of China (PBOC) for bank counterparty verification, and by SAMR for one-company-one-address consistency. The statutory interpretation requires a physical address with possessory right, a company name plate, staff presence, and evidence of actual operational activity. Shared-office or serviced-office space that includes a designated physical suite number, a lease agreement, and on-site reception area is acceptable, provided the lease term is at least one year and the address is not used solely as a mail-forwarding service.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) possession of an authentic lease deed for the registered address; (2) on-site name plate of the WFOE; (3) presence of goods display, inventory storage, or office facilities appropriate for e-commerce retail; (4) utility bills (electricity, water, internet) consistent with the registered address; (5) letterbox and corporate seal custody records; (6) compliance with tax bureau's on-site verification rules for newly registered VAT enterprises. Quantified risk: moderate and upward if a virtual office is detected; unannounced physical inspection probability is estimated at 15% during the first four months, rising to 30% if the address appears on the SAMR abnormal business directory or is flagged by tax authorities as a multi-tenant mail box.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024), Articles 23-27, 32, 35-36, 38, 41-42, 47, 50-51, 59, 67-68, 83, and 89; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4, 5, and 31; Regulations on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (State Council Decree No. 746), Articles 2, 8, 10, 12, 15, and 17
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Enterprise Registration Bureau of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), acting through the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) of the city of establishment and the relevant Municipal Government Integrated Service Window
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application Form for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, submitted together with the Foreign Investment Information Report through the SAMR National Enterprise Registration and Filing Portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a WFOE limited liability company engaged in online retail under ISIC 4791, and no blocked escrow account is required. Under the 2023 PRC Company Law, the subscribed capital must be paid in full within five years from establishment unless a shorter term is fixed in the Articles of Association. Contributions may be in cash or in non-cash assets permitted by law. The registered capital amount should be commercially reasonable and consistent with the projected business scale, banking requirements, tax filings, and annual reporting obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, as the first written resolution of the Board of Directors of the foreign-invested limited liability company to be established as a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (the Company), acting by unanimous consent, as follows:

1. Share Capital Subscription. The registered capital of the Company shall be [●] RMB, divided into [●] ordinary shares with a par value of [●] RMB per share. The subscription made by the sole shareholder for all such shares in the amount of [●] RMB, payable in accordance with the Articles of Association, is approved, ratified, and accepted. The legal representative is directed to execute the subscription documents, open a dedicated capital contribution account in the name of the Company, and ensure that each contribution is recorded in the Company's accounting books no later than the statutory deadline under the Company Law. No return of contribution or reduction of capital shall be made except by a further resolution and statutory filing.

2. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Company is fixed and adopted at [●], China. This address shall be the Company's statutory seat, registered address for service of process, and domicile for administrative notices. The legal representative is authorized to execute the lease agreement, obtain the landlord's title certificate, and file the address confirmation with the local Administration for Market Regulation.

3. Banking Authorization. The Company shall open RMB and, if needed, foreign currency bank accounts with [●] Bank, and the bank signatory forms shall list [Name], [Name], and [Name] with the signature authority specified in the bank mandate. The Board authorizes the legal representative to present this Resolution, the Articles of Association, and the business license to the bank and to complete account activation. Any change to the authorized signatory matrix shall require a subsequent Board resolution.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The Company hereby appoints [Name] as Executive Director and General Manager, [Name] as Supervisor, and [Name] as the legal representative of the Company. Each appointee accepts the duties of integrity and diligence set out in the Company Law and shall act in compliance with the Articles of Association. The legal representative is authorized to execute all contracts, filings, and registrations necessary to give effect to the incorporation and operation of the Company.

5. General Authorization. The Executive Director and General Manager are jointly and severally authorized to take all lawful actions, sign and notarize documents, pay fees, and make all filings directed by the formation plan, provided that no action outside the ordinary course of business or requiring a shareholder resolution is taken without further shareholder approval. This Resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name pre-approval and filing of the application for establishment registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) Market Entity Registration Division, through the SAMR National Enterprise Registration and Filing Portal or the municipal government integrated online service platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name pre-approval application for the proposed WFOE name in the format [City + Brand + Industry + Limited Company]. After obtaining name approval, prepare and execute the Articles of Association, convene the first shareholders' decision and first board resolution, and submit the establishment registration application with electronic signatures of the sole shareholder, executive director, supervisor, and legal representative. The Hong Kong parent company's certificate of incorporation, certificate of change of name, and current director and shareholder registers must be notarized by a Hong Kong notary public recognized by the PRC Ministry of Justice and transmitted to the mainland registration authority. The authority will verify the lease, legal representative identity, and business scope, and will issue the business license if the application is complete.
required_dossiers: Notarized and legally transmitted certificate of incorporation of the Hong Kong shareholder
Notarized current director and shareholder registers of the Hong Kong shareholder
Certificate of change of name (if applicable) with notarized Chinese translation
Power of attorney appointing the local formation agent
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Shareholders' resolutions and the First Board of Directors Resolution
Lease agreement and landlord ownership certificate for the registered office
Identity certificate or passport of the appointed legal representative
Identity certificate of the executive director, general manager, and supervisor
Foreign Investment Information Report data sheet
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AMR issues a correction list, respond and re-submit the amended electronic forms within 5 business days; correct any inconsistency between the Articles, board resolution, or address proof. If the registered name is rejected for duplicate or prohibited characters, select a new name and restart the pre-approval process; no additional notarization is required for a name-only refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign investment information reporting and negative list compliance screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce of the People's Republic of China (MOFCOM) and the provincial commerce department, using the integrated Foreign Investment Information Report module within the SAMR portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Foreign Investment Information Report simultaneously with the establishment registration by submitting the beneficial ownership, ultimate parent company, business scope, and investment structure data. Confirm that an online retail business for portable power products under ISIC 4791 does not appear in the Foreign Investment Negative List; if the activity is outside the negative list, no MOFCOM approval is required and the filing is recorded automatically. If the Hong Kong shareholder is ultimately controlled by a Chinese resident or an entity in a restricted sector, perform a red-flag review of the actual controller. After approval, retain the registration receipt and include the foreign investment information in the annual report.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Information Report form
Articles of Association
Certificate of business license or pre-registration approval
Notarized identity/ownership documents of the ultimate beneficial owner
Foreign Investment Negative List compliance statement
Organizational chart showing the HK parent and the mainland WFOE
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOFCOM or the AMR queries the report, submit a written explanation and corrected data within 30 days under the Measures for Foreign Investment Information Reporting. If the actual controller is found to be inaccurate, the WFOE should file an amended report; if the negative list review identifies a restricted sector, the business scope must be revised before the license is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business license issuance, company seal carving, and formal governance record creation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR) for license issuance; Municipal Public Security Bureau for seal carve registration and record filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After payment of no state registration fee and completion of all checks, the AMR issues the WFOE's Business License bearing the unified social credit code. Immediately thereafter, obtain the official company seal, legal representative seal, financial seal, and invoice seal from a licensed seal engraving company, and file the seal signatures with the Public Security Bureau. Record the issued registered capital, shareholders, directors, legal representative, and registered office in the Company's statutory books, keeping the First Board Resolution and Articles of Association as originals in the registered office. This step also triggers the WFOE's existence as a legal person from the date of license issuance, permitting pre-incorporation contracts to be ratified.
required_dossiers: Business License original
Unified social credit code certificate
Articles of Association and First Board Resolution
Legal representative identity card
Application form for seal engraving and filing
Address certificate and lease confirmation
Board resolution authorizing seal application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the seal-engraving company refuses the order due to incomplete filing, apply to the Public Security Bureau for a formal seal record certificate and re-present the business license. If there is any discrepancy in the license data, use the AMR data correction procedure within 7 days; do not use the license for banking until the correction is completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, social insurance, foreign exchange, and employment registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local State Taxation Administration (STA) office for tax registration; municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau for social insurance and housing fund filing; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the designated bank for foreign currency account registration; local statistical office for statistical registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the multi-reporting registration through the national one-stop government platform so that tax, social insurance, statistics, and housing fund records are linked to the unified social credit code. Determine the applicable tax registration procedure, select a tax representative, and decide whether to be a general VAT taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer considering the expected online retail revenue. Review customs import/export registration if the solar panels and portable power products will be imported or exported across the China border. Register the legal representative and employees for social insurance and open the employer housing fund account. If the Company maintains foreign currency accounts, complete SAFE foreign exchange registration through the bank and submit the board banking authorization.
required_dossiers: Business License original and copy
Unified social credit code certificate
Articles of Association and First Board Resolution
Legal representative identity card
Lease agreement and venue proof
Tax registration and taxpayer status application form
Social insurance registration form
Housing fund enrollment form
Foreign exchange registration application and bank account mandate
Customs registration form if cross-border trade is intended
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority issues a notice of inquiry, respond through the electronic tax bureau within 15 days and provide the revised business scope or revenue forecast. For social insurance objections, correct the employee headcount and payroll data. If the SAFE bank rejects the foreign currency account application, amend the board banking authorization to address the signature requirements, and re-present the registration documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account activation, capital contribution deposit, and post-incorporation regulatory filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank selected in the Board Resolution; local AMR for record and filing changes; national enterprise credit information publicity system for annual reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the Business License, Articles, First Board Resolution, and seal to the bank to open the RMB basic account and, if applicable, the foreign currency capital account. Deposit the subscribed capital into the Company's basic account in accordance with the payment schedule and update the accounting records. Prepare a bank mandate that expressly lists each authorized officer and the joint or several signature requirement. File the opening of the basic account with the People's Bank of China's account management system through the bank, and record the capital contribution ledger. After all licenses and accounts are in operation, the WFOE should convene a post-incorporation board meeting to ratify expenses, select the tax accounting software, adopt internal controls, and fix the initial audit and filing calendar. The WFOE must thereafter file the annual report with SAMR before June 30 each year and maintain the corporate records for at least 15 years.
required_dossiers: Business License original and copy
Unified social credit code certificate
Company seal, legal representative seal, financial seal, and invoice seal
First Board Resolution and banking authorization
Articles of Association
Legal representative and authorized officer identity documents
Tax registration certificate and tax filing confirmation
Foreign Investment Information Report filing receipt
Capital contribution schedule and bank payment voucher
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional proof of beneficial ownership, submit the anti-money laundering statement and the ownership chart. If the capital contribution payment is delayed beyond the five-year statutory period, the board must adopt a revised schedule and file a capital change registration with the AMR; consider a reduction of registered capital if the full subscription amount is not commercially supportable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 4791 is non-store online retail rather than manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing (ISIC 1xxx/2xxx/3xxx/4xxx/52xx), so no industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over the stated retail activity; if the Company later establishes a physical warehouse or battery assembly operation, the municipal Administration for Emergency Management becomes the competent authority for dangerous substance and fire safety approval.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial production license is required under the Catalogue of Industrial Product Production License Administration for the pure online resale of portable solar power products; ordinary e-commerce retail is subject only to market entity registration and the general product quality and e-commerce laws.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) of the People's Republic of China and the provincial ecology and environment bureau - only if physical construction or scale-up occurs
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Environmental Registration not required for pure online retail and office operations with no pollutant discharge, no chemical processing, no assembly line, and no regulated construction that could trigger an EIA category; if a fulfillment warehouse for portable battery generators is established, the operator must conduct a Classified Management Checklist environmental assessment under the EIA Law to determine whether a full EIA Report, EIA Report Form, or Registration Form is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable for the current online retail scope. If future warehousing or assembly of lithium-ion products is introduced, the operator shall comply with the Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard (GB 8978-1996), Emission Standards for Odor Pollutants (GB 14554-93), and the General Industrial Solid Waste Storage and Disposal Site Pollution Control Standard (GB 18599-2020), together with hazardous waste transfer manifest obligations under the Solid Waste Law if damaged battery modules are discarded.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial civil-defense permit for the pure online retail business. The office or light commercial premises must still comply with the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China and the workplace safety obligations under the Work Safety Law; if the leased premises are required to have a fire safety inspection or filing, the landlord or occupier shall obtain the Fire Safety Inspection Certificate from the local Fire and Rescue Department. In any future battery/solar panel warehouse, a Fire Safety Approval (civil defense clearance) would be mandatory, including compliance with lithium battery storage codes, separation distances, extinguishing systems, and employee occupational hazard notification under the Occupational Disease Prevention and Control Law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; electronic clearance and self-service registration portal: the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) under the STA, accessible via provincial State Tax Service platforms with full integration into the Golden Tax-IV digital monitoring system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) as a limited liability company with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the business license containing the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). Step 2: Within thirty calendar days of the business license issuance, complete tax registration information confirmation through the Electronic Tax Bureau; the USCC is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and is also used for enterprise income tax, VAT, stamp duty, and withholding tax accounts. Step 3: Register the foreign dominant management facts and bank account details; for general taxpayer status, submit the VAT general taxpayer registration if annual taxable sales are expected to exceed CNY 5,000,000 or elect voluntary registration if annual sales are below that threshold. Step 4: Complete the export tax rebate (exemption) recordal, i.e., export tax refund qualification filing, in the e-Tax export tax module before claiming zero-rating. Step 5: Register as a foreign trade operator with the local Department of Commerce and file an enterprise customs registration/declaration filing with the competent Customs district. Step 6: Complete trade-in-goods foreign exchange operations qualification with a designated foreign exchange bank under SAFE's trade-in-goods truth-verification system. No additional physical TIN card is issued; the business license and tax registration information confirmation record are the official tax identity evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity level classification. The PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law does not recognize check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections; a WFOE is automatically a Chinese tax resident enterprise. In VAT, the only election available is choice of small-scale taxpayer classification for annual taxable sales below CNY 5,000,000 or voluntary general taxpayer status, subject to accounting capability and input-output invoice management requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) administered under the Interim Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Value-Added Tax and the Notification on the Implementation of the VAT Reform; export sales are governed by the Measures for the Administration of Export Tax Refund (Exemption).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales is the threshold above which VAT general taxpayer registration becomes mandatory; below CNY 5,000,000 the WFOE may retain small-scale taxpayer status. Irrespective of turnover, tax registration must be completed within 30 days of the business license issuance, so the economic threshold does not relieve a newly formed WFOE from initial tax registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The Golden Tax-IV system requires real-time transmission of special VAT invoice details to the STA invoice verification platform. Invoices must be issued through the official e-Tax electronic invoice service or an STA-approved tax control U-Key device. Comprehensive digitalized electronic invoices carry a statutory invoice number, QR code, and tax-control metadata; red-letter invoice substitution is only permitted through the e-Tax system. Enterprises must match electronic invoice data with customs export declarations, export proceeds data, and logistics data before export tax refund claims; anti-fraud screening applies to invoice frequency, counterparty risk, commodity tax classifications, price anomalies, and transport-geolocation consistency.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registered VAT general taxpayer WFOE engaged in the e-commerce export of portable battery generators and solar panels may claim zero-rating where: (i) the goods are actually exported from the customs territory through a customs export declaration under the applicable e-commerce supervision code, such as 9610 for cross-border e-commerce retail export, 9710 for B2B direct export, or 9810 for overseas warehouse export; (ii) the underlying export order, logistics record, and payment flow can be matched on a one-to-one basis; (iii) the goods are new, materially conform to the documented product description and customs commodity classification, and are sold to an overseas buyer outside mainland China; (iv) the export proceeds are repatriated into a China-designated bank in foreign currency or RMB under an approved cross-border settlement arrangement; and (v) the input VAT has been lawfully certified. Qualifying offshore digital services are not relevant to this goods-export WFOE.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs Declaration Form for Exported Goods) containing the export supervision code and the verified product HS classification
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, cross-border vehicle manifest, or international consignment note proving physical departure from the PRC customs territory
Export invoice (commercial invoice) issued by the WFOE to the overseas customer

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank export proceeds receipt confirmation showing receipt of foreign exchange; for e-commerce platform sales, the payment settlement report and foreign exchange settlement record must be provided
Export contract or electronic purchase order and payment terms
VAT special invoices of domestic suppliers for purchased inventory and input services
Packing list, logistics waybill, and e-commerce platform transaction data supporting the three-flow consistency of order flow, logistics flow, and payment flow
SAFE trade-in-goods external payment/collection declaration record and the export tax rebate electronic declaration file
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export tax refund claims are subject to the STA's classified export-tax-rebate management categories I-IV, which determine the intensity of document review and on-site inspection. If the STA or customs determines that the zero-rating was based on fictitious export orders, false customs declarations, recycled goods, falsified transport or exchange settlement documents, or failure to repatriate proceeds within the required 180-day period unless duly registered as an exception, the refund/zero-rating will be reversed, the underlying input credits will be clawed back, and overdue interest will be imposed under the Tax Collection and Administration Law. Administrative penalties may range from 50 percent to 500 percent of the tax involved; the WFOE may be disqualified from export tax rebate treatment for a period of 6 months to 3 years; and in severe cases, criminal liability for false export tax refunds under Articles 201 and 204 of the Criminal Law can lead to fines and imprisonment. Retrospective review periods extend to 3 years for ordinary adjustments, 5 years for special circumstances, and an unlimited period for deliberate evasion, fraud, or withholding on non-resident payments.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) under Companies Ordinance Cap 622
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days after each anniversary of incorporation; annual recurrence on the incorporation anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee escalates from HKD 1,050 (over 42 days up to 3 months), HKD 2,100 (over 3 months up to 6 months), to HKD 3,500 (over 6 months). The company and responsible persons may be prosecuted with fines up to HKD 50,000 plus HKD 1,000 per day for continuing default; the Registrar may apply for administrative strike-off under Cap 622 s.746 after persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate renewal (annual business registration fee and insolvency levy)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, no later than the expiry date; renewal must be applied for within the one-month period before the expiration of the current certificate.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a valid Business Registration Certificate is an offence, carrying a fine of up to HKD 5,000 and imprisonment for up to six months; outstanding fees and levies are subject to collection, and the IRD may pursue compulsory deregistration or recovery proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (BIR51) with audited financial statements and tax computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due within one month of the issue date shown on the return; for annual block-issued returns with a 31 December year-end, the eTax extended due date is typically 15 May, and tax representatives may receive further blanket extensions as published by the IRD.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may lead to an estimated assessment under IRO s.59(3), penalties of up to HKD 10,000 under IRO s.80, and an additional 10% tax on understated assessable profits under IRO s.82A, together with prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (BIR56A and BIR56B forms) where any employee is remunerated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR (Employer's Return Unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually as stated on the issued return, generally within one month of issue; the IRD issues the annual employer return in early April, and the standard due date is usually 1 May or 2 May unless an extension is granted.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to furnish the return without reasonable excuse is an offence under IRO s.80, with a maximum fine of HKD 10,000 and a daily penalty for continuing default; prosecution and estimated assessments may follow.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Hong Kong Companies Ordinance Cap 622, every active company incorporated in Hong Kong must have its financial statements audited annually by a practicing certified public accountant; there is no turnover, total assets, or employee headcount threshold that exempts an active company from statutory audit. A dormant company may pass a special resolution to dispense with an audit if it has no significant accounting transactions. For Companies Registry delivery, a private company qualifies as a 'small private company' only if it satisfies at least two of three conditions: total revenue not exceeding HKD 100 million, total assets not exceeding HKD 100 million, and not more than 100 employees. A non-small private company must deliver its audited financial statements and directors' and auditors' reports to the Companies Registry in addition to the annual return. The statutory audit must be performed by an independent certifying CPA licensed under the Professional Accountants Ordinance Cap 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are fully converged with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS); eligible non-public entities may apply the HKFRS for Private Entities, and any election must be applied consistently. Financial statements must give a true and fair view under Cap 622 and be accompanied by a directors' report and an independent auditor's report.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong law does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation to be filed with the

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: High-tech enterprise reduced rate 15%; small low-profit enterprise incremental deductions; R&D super-deduction 100% (200% of qualifying R&D costs); no patent box in mainland China, but free-trade zone pilot policies may apply

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form A110000) filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration (STA) e-Tax portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional returns during the year)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be submitted within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (May 31 for calendar-year taxpayers); quarterly returns due within 15 days after each quarter

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Revenue: turnover from online retail of solar portable power stations, generators, and ancillary solar panels net of allowances, discounts, and returns
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise revenue from all global sales channels including Stripe and Affirm BNPL; if the WFOE contracts with overseas consumers, report full gross considerations; reconcile FX conversion differences at the central parity rate; do not net out platform commissions or payment gateway fees

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Cost: cost of goods sold directly attributable to solar products and accessories sold, including inbound logistics, duties, and warehousing
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Match cost of inventory using weighted average costing; if purchases are made from a Hong Kong affiliate, ensure the transfer price reflects the arm's length principle and that intercompany purchase invoices are supported by contemporaneous documentation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Profit (accounting profit): comprehensive income from all sources computed under PRC Accounting Standards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back accrued but unaudited items such as investment revaluation surpluses and foreign exchange gains; dividend income received from foreign subsidiaries may require exemption or foreign tax credit handling; if the WFOE is a pure retailer, ensure no offshore branch profits are wrongly omitted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Adjusted Income after net addition/adjustment items from Schedule A105000
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add prohibited deductions (penalties, excessive entertainment, unrelated sponsorship) and subtract tax-exempt items (e.g., treasury bond interest); clearly reflect any merry-go-round or circular transaction adjustments if intercompany payments were recharacterised by the tax authority

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income after offsetting previous-year losses (carryforward maximum 5 years)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward applies to the WFOE's own losses, not group losses; if a merger or restructuring occurred, follow special reorganisation rules; for non-resident investor, no allocation of income is allowed unless a permanent establishment exists in China

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income Tax Payable calculated at 25% on taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the WFOE is eligible for a reduced rate (e.g., 15% high-tech certification), compute using the reduced rate; if foreign tax credits are claimed for Hong Kong or overseas tax paid, attach appropriate certificates; ensure quarterly prepayments have been correctly credited

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Deductions and Exemption Amount: preferential reductions, plus credits for purchase of environmental equipment and R&D super-deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the amount that reduces the computed tax (e.g., difference between 25% and preferential 15% rate); R&D super-deduction must be evidenced by an R&D project ledger; do not claim any tax holiday unless the entity operates in a statutory free-trade zone with explicit approval

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net Income Tax Payable for the year, i.e., Box 6 minus Box 7 and any tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: After filing, if the WFOE distributes dividends to its Hong Kong parent, the withholding tax obligation arises separately at the time of distribution; Box 8 must not be reduced by the 10% (or treaty 5%) withholding tax applicable to outbound dividends; that withholding is collected when dividends are declared

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total tax due after prior-year overpayments and quarterly prepayments; settlement amount to be paid with the return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure bank account used for e-payment is the WFOE's China bank account; any overpayment may be carried forward or refunded; if the tax authority has already issued an audit adjustment notice, reflect the resulting amount here

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary information on related-party transactions (attached to annual return)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare all intercompany sales, purchases, royalties, and service fees with the Hong Kong parent and any other affiliates; attach the Company-wide Related-Party Transaction Summary Table; failure to disclose or inaccurate disclosure triggers separate transfer-pricing penalties

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: RMB 2,000 flat fine per return, plus daily surcharge of 0.05% of outstanding tax for late payment; failure to pay after demand triggers enforcement measures (seizure of assets, bank account freeze); false or fraudulent returns cause a civil penalty of 50% to 500% of the unpaid tax under Tax Collection Administration Law Article 63 and criminal liability at RMB 50,000 (or 10% of total tax) threshold under Criminal Law Article 201

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividend distributions to non-resident corporate shareholders; reduced to 5% if the Chinese-Hong Kong DTA applies and the beneficial owner is a Hong Kong resident company directly holding at least 25% of the dividend-paying company's share capital
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain the 5% treaty rate, the Hong Kong parent must (i) file the Non-resident Enterprise Enjoying Tax Treaty Treatment Report (Form 1100) with the Chinese tax authority before or no later than the date of dividend distribution; (ii) provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department for the relevant calendar year; (iii) substantiate beneficial ownership via a declaration and supporting evidence that the Hong Kong company has economic substance (employees, office, decision-making) and is not a conduit; (iv) ensure the WFOE has not already withheld the statutory 10% - if it has, a refund can be claimed through the tax authority's te-return mechanism within 3 years. The treaty claim is subject to anti-abuse rules under STA Announcement 2018/9.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 10%, treaty rate 7% under the China-HK DTA; Royalties: statutory 10%, treaty rate 7% under the China-HK DTA for industrial, commercial or scientific royalties; both require the same beneficial ownership documentation as dividends and must be satisfied at the time of each payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when annual intercompany transactions exceed: RMB 20 million for transfers of tangible assets, RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers, RMB 100 million for intangible asset transfers, or RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions (including services). Master File is required if the total related-party revenue exceeds RMB 1 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mainland China has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations, but the WFOE must demonstrate physical presence (office, staff, management decisions) in China to rebut any sham or agency characterisation; the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) concept applies to the Hong Kong parent for treaty claims, and China's de facto management test and General Anti-Avoidance Rule (CIT Law Article 47) require that intercompany transactions reflect real economic functions and risk assumption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining dual bookkeeping or diverting e-commerce proceeds from Stripe/Affirm to offshore personal accounts, thus underreporting gross receipts and evading corporate income tax and dividend withholding tax on remittances to the Hong Kong shareholder.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL) Article 63: confiscation of illegal gains, order to repay the evaded tax, late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and a civil fine between 50% and 500% of the evaded tax amount. Criminal Law Article 201: if the evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and constitutes more than 10% of total tax payable, imprisonment up to 3 years; if the amount is huge and exceeds 30%, imprisonment up to 7 years, plus fines and forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct or participate in the offshore diversion are personally and jointly liable for the tax deficiency, fines, and unpaid WHT; the court may pierce the corporate veil and attach personal assets of the legal representative and CFO; a travel ban (exit denial) is imposed under TCAL Article 44; criminal conviction can result in 3–7 years’ imprisonment and debarment from holding directorships.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misreporting and Lack of Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring artificially low sales prices to the Hong Kong affiliate, making excessive interest-free loans or shell royalty payments to shift profits out of China, and failing to prepare a Local File or Master File within the statutory time limits despite exceeding the RMB 40 million threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT Law Article 41 (arm’s length principle) and Article 48 (special tax adjustment); STA Announcement 2016/42 issuances: the tax authority may recharacterise the transaction and impose an interest charge on the additional tax equal to the benchmark lending rate plus 5 percentage points. If inaccurate documentation is deemed a false submission, TCAL penalties of 50%–5x unpaid tax may apply, and under Criminal Law Article 201 fraudulent means to evade tax are prosecutable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or approve false transfer pricing documentation are exposed to personal liability for the additional tax and interest if the corporate veil is lifted; travel restrictions and asset freezes can be ordered; a director who intentionally causes under-reporting is similarly exposed to criminal liability under Article 201, with imprisonment up to 7 years in egregious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Abuse / Shell Company Lack of Beneficial Ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting up a Hong Kong strip-company with no office, employees, or business functions, interposed solely to invoice solar product sales and to claim the 5% dividend WHT treaty rate or the 7% royalty/interest rates while all substantive decisions are made in China.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: STA Announcement 2018/9 (Measures for the Administration of Non-resident Enterprises Enjoying Tax Treaty Treatment): denial of treaty benefits and recovery of the additional withholding tax (e.g., from 5% to 10%) plus late-payment interest; General Anti-Avoidance Rule (CIT Law Article 47) allows re-computation of the income as belonging to the Chinese WFOE and re-assesses tax. Civil fines under TCAL Article 44 for fraudulent reporting and issuance of false certifications may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who orchestrate the shell arrangement are personally liable for the under-withheld tax if the structure is disregarded and the corporate veil is pierced; a blacklisting (travel ban) and bank seizure order can be issued; criminal penalties for fraudulent use of tax treaties can extend to imprisonment up to 3 years for evidence forgery under Criminal Law Article 280, plus restitution of the full tax shortfall.
